full_text:
2/19/26 4:05 AM

Description:

Page 2 of 4

I scheduled an intake via telehealth with Dr.
Inderpreet Virk, operating as the lead
psychiatrist for Brain Health USA. | sought
care based on the clinic's explicit
advertisements stating they specialize in
complex substance issues and
benzodiazepine tapering. | presented seeking
a safe, medically supervised taper off of
street-sourced Xanax (historically up to
22mg, at the time of meeting, 6mg).

Despite being a Board-Certified Addiction
Psychiatrist, Dr. Virk exhibited a severe
departure from the standard of care:

Refusal to Treat / Patient Abandonment: Dr.
Virk explicitly refused to initiate a standard
medical tapering protocol, stating my case
was "too much of a liability" and a "sticky
situation" because my prior usage was
street-sourced and lacked pharmaceutical
documentation. Refusing to medically
manage a patient actively seeking to
transition from illicit benzodiazepines to safe
medical oversight—while knowing the fatal
risks of abrupt benzodiazepine
withdrawal—constitutes gross negligence
and a fundamental failure to perform the
duties of an addiction specialist.

Misleading Advertising (Bait-and-Switch):
Brain Health USA specifically advertises
specialized benzodiazepine tapering to Medi-
Cal/L.A. Care patients. However, their lead
addiction psychiatrist outright refuses to
treat patients with a history of street
procurement, which encompasses a massive
demographic of the addiction population
they claim to serve.

Substandard Psychiatric Assessment: After
denying primary care for the benzodiazepine
dependency, Dr. Virk reluctantly prescribed a
10-day Suboxone bridge at my desperate
request. He then concluded the session by
rapidly asking if | felt suicidal or felt like
hurting or others, utilizing a dismissive,
“box-checking" approach to a severe
psychiatric safety assessment for a highly
vulnerable patient he had just denied
comprehensive care to.

| request the Board investigate Dr. Virk’s
refusal to provide standard addiction
medicine care, his patient abandonment due
to "liability," and the misleading nature of the
clinic's advertised specialties.
